chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb al-Naysaburi, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not fast on the day of Ashura, nor on the day of Arafat, in Mecca, nor in Medina, nor in your hometown, nor in any of the cities.

key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: Arafat, the 9th day of Dhu al-Hijjah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting on Ashura and Arafat in Mecca and Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling on fasting during the days of Ashura and Arafat when one is not in the state of Hajj, distinguishing between obligatory and recommended fasting in specific locations like Mecca, Medina, and one's hometown. Shia scholars interpret this to mean that while fasting on these days is generally recommended (mustahabb) for those in their hometowns or other cities, it is prohibited for those performing Hajj in Mecca or residing in Medina, as the rituals of Hajj take precedence. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding voluntary fasting based on geographical and ritual context.
